title: Slotline staffing allocator and scoped-prune protocol proposal
creator: Nina Park
description:
Problem: As we scale Redwood Dedicated and Private customer commitments, PMs and Eng leads are spending >6h/week manually slicing cycles. Current tranche playbooks are qualitative and often yield uneven critical-path coverage, late firefighting, and surprise over-allocations for hot features.

Goal: Define and pilot a lightweight operational pattern and an accompanying slotline allocator — a deterministic, prioritized staffing allocator + scope-pruning protocol that converts initiative priorities, role availability, and risk buffers into a concrete two-week staffing slate. The output should be a ranked list of scope items with recommended FTE fraction, a fallback scope list, and a minimal handoff plan for cross-team dependencies.

Scope: This ticket covers product definition, acceptance criteria, coordination with Eng for a prototype allocator script, and a decision memo for leadership. Implementation of the allocator in tooling (dashboard/automation) is out of scope for this ticket and will be a follow-up if pilot is accepted.

Key constraints and desiderata:
- Low cognitive overhead for PMs (target: <30 minutes to run a slate exercise)
- Transparent, auditable rules that can be reviewed by Eng leads and applied to Dedicated/DL customers
- Prioritizes reliability-critical work and SLA-bound initiatives over exploratory/market-research tasks
- Provides a soft buffer ("rolling negative-scope") that can be reclaimed without team context switching penalty

Deliverables:
1) Protocol doc (Confluence link) describing inputs, rules, and examples
2) Prototype allocator script (Python notebook + README) that ingests a CSV of role availability and initiative ranks and outputs staffing slates
3) Decision memo for Exec summarizing trade-offs and pilot success criteria
4) Pilot run notes and retrospective with two cross-functional teams (Search infra + Console UX)

Links to artifacts:
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/slotline-allocator-draft
- Prototype repo (internal): https://github.com/redwood-inference/cycle-tools/tree/slotline-allocator
- Example GA dashboard (cost/latency impact): https://dash.redwood.ai/d/capacity/slotline-demo
- Reference playbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1SlotlinePlaybookExample

Tradeoffs considered:
- Deterministic ranking vs. probabilistic Monte Carlo capacity simulation: we choose deterministic with clear guardrails for the MVP to reduce PM overhead and increase reproducibility.
- Strict FTE enforcement vs. soft recommendations: MVP will emit recommended FTE fractions and a confidence band (high/medium/low) rather than hard assignments to avoid blocking managers' autonomy.

Success metrics (pilot):
- Time-to-produce a staffing slate: target median <= 30 minutes
- Percentage of pilot slates that require <2 tactical reassignments after execution window: target >= 70%
- Reduction in cross-team urgent rework incidents attributable to overcommit: target 30% reduction vs. last cycle
- PM/Eng perceived clarity score (post-pilot survey): target >= 4/5

Acceptance criteria:
- Protocol doc reviewed and approved by at least two Eng leads and two PMs
- Prototype script runs end-to-end with synthetic and real cycle inputs and produces human-readable slate CSVs and a short rationale blob per slot
- Pilot retrospective recorded with action items and a recommendation to A) proceed to automate; or B) iterate on ruleset (with specific changes)

Implementation notes for Eng collaboration:
- Prototype will depend on canonical role availability feed (ENG-21984). If feed is incomplete, fallback to manual CSV input for pilot.
- The allocator will include a "risk score" heuristic combining customer_SLA, dependency_count, and estimated engineering uncertainty. Each heuristic component documented in Appendix A of Confluence doc.

Rollout plan for pilot:
- Week 1: Walkthrough with pilot teams; collect role availability CSVs; run allocator in war-room with PM+Eng leads
- Week 2: Teams execute two-week slate; PMs collect feedback and operational friction points
- Week 3: Postmortem & decision memo to Leadership

Longer-term follow-ups (outside this ticket):
- Dashboard integration for one-click re-run (Console team), automated role feeds, and an API endpoint to provision temporary burst capacity for Dedicated customers.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol doc approved by >=2 Eng leads and 2 PMs; prototype produces readable slate CSVs from sample inputs; pilot retrospective with action items and a clear recommendation to automate or iterate.
notes: This is intentionally scoped to product definition + prototype. Eng implementation effort and console integration will be a subsequent ticket. We will try to reuse the role feed from ENG-21984 to minimize manual inputs.
